text:
Alex: FYI I'm kicking off an RFC thread for a non-functional 'fallthrough routing' playbook for customer-managed VPCs/on-prem. Goal: define acceptance criteria + rollback/playbook for when customer routing makes our control or data plane unreachable.

Maria: +1. We need to be explicit about graceful degradation vs full cutover. Is MVP only detection+alerting, or automated fallback too?

Alex: For MVP I propose: 1) automatic detection + alert; 2) automated soft-fallback (route to hosted-compatible model variant) behind a kill-switch; 3) operator runbook for full failover. Automated hard failover is deferred.

Sanjay: Can we enumerate failure modes? Off the top: route deletion, asymmetric routing, BGP session flap, egress NAT change, DNS split-horizon divergence, MTU drop.

Priya: Add: partial packet loss (ECMP causing 5-25% packet loss), and transient blackholing during config pushes. Also IPv6-specific NAT behavior.

Jordan: Edge case: customer has stateful firewall that drops requests with source IP not in their whitelist after we change egress. Playbook should include rekey/whitelist handshake steps.

Maria: Acceptance criteria draft: 
- Detection: system detects >5% 5-minute request failure rate to private control plane endpoints OR BGP session down for >2m.
- Alerting: P1 alert to oncall + slack #customer-x channel within 2m.
- Soft-fallback: route requests to hosted inference variant with verified compatibility 95% of time during test canary.
- Traceability: every fallback event must create an audit entry with customer id, reason code, and egress IP.

Alex: +1. Also add SLO guardrails: fallback allowed only when latency increase <2x and cost delta <3x, unless customer opts-in.

Sanjay: For tests, we should simulate: 
1) BGP flap (terminate session)
2) Blackhole route (netns ip route replace to unreachable)
3) Egress IP swap (NAT translation change)
4) DNS split-horizon mismatch (return internal IP)
We should run these against a staging connector that mirrors prod config.

Priya: Implementation notes: 
- Detector: controlplane healthcheck + passive request success ratio + BGP telemetry.
- Policy engine: policy per-customer with three actions {alert-only, soft-fallback, disallow-fallback}.
- Safe-mode: a manual override in Console and an API endpoint `POST /customers/:id/fallback/force` guarded by 2FA.

Jordan: Security/keys: if control plane becomes unreachable we must avoid exposing KMS material. Ensure any hosted fallback only uses models with no customer-specific keys or data in cache. Document this in the playbook.

Alex: Good catch. Add acceptance: hosted fallback must not access customer private mounts or KMS-protected resources.

deploy-bot: RFC draft created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/edge-fallthrough-routing (draft) :page_facing_up:

Maria: Launch criteria proposal: 
- Implementation complete in staging + runbook written (docs + runbook steps)
- 3 blackout simulations passed without data leakage
- Oncall training + runbook tabletop exercise completed with at least 2 engineers
- Canary release to 10% of connectors for non-prod customers for 2 weeks with monitoring dashboards

Sanjay: Rollback triggers for fallback: 
- Fallback causes >10% functional regressions in outputs (evaluated via smoke prompt suite)
- Latency spike >3x baseline for >10m
- Any sign of unauthorized data access or KMS error
If triggered, system should automatically revert to customer-managed routing and page oncall.

Priya: Ops playbook skeleton (short): 
1) Triage alert -> run `check-bgp.sh <customer>` (script)
2) Validate egress ip with `dig +short myip.example.com` from connector
3) If blackholed: engage customer network lead and execute agreed NAT/ACL rollback
4) If BGP flap: attempt BGP session re-establish with incremental backoff (1m, 2m, 5m)
5) If cannot recover in 15m and policy allows: enable soft-fallback and monitor

Alex: Ownership and prioritization: this is customer-driven for enterprise tier; recommend prioritized for Q2 due to several customers requesting onprem stability guarantees. Scope for v1: detection+alerts+soft-fallback+runbook+canary. Defer: automated hard failover, multi-region cross-customer routing.

Jordan: Docs note: include explicit edge case: customer NATs egress IP per-subnet so egress IPs can rotate — need to define acceptable TTL and detection window to avoid flapping.

Maria: Dev tasks I'd assign: 
- Detector + telemetry (Sanjay)
- Policy engine + API (Priya)
- Runbook + tabletop (Jordan + Alex)
- Console flags + canary UI (Alex)
- Data/telemetry retention for audit logs (Maria)

Alex: Timeline suggestion: 3-week sprint for detector+telemetry, 2-week sprint for policy+API, then 2 weeks for runbook+canary. Total ~7 weeks to canary.

Sanjay: One more edge: asymmetric routing causing TCP RSTs — we should prefer stateless healthchecks (HTTP 1xx/2xx) over TCP-only to avoid false positives.

Priya: Agreed. Also: add a 'quiet window' after connector config pushes where detector tolerates short blips (5m) to reduce noise.

Jordan: I'll draft the runbook doc and post link here. Also will schedule a 45m tabletop for Wed.

Alex: Thanks everyone. Action items: Sanjay start detector prototype; Priya start policy schema; Jordan + Alex runbook draft; Maria prepare audit retention plan. We'll reconvene after tabletop. :thumbsup:
